task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about a nonprofit's purchase of the former Brook Lantern Motel for housing. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 17, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Alder Key Housing Trust completed its purchase of the closed Brook Lantern Motel on Sept. 16, 2026.
The $1.8 million purchase was financed with a $1.2 million housing grant and $600,000 from the trust's designated acquisition fund.
The motel has 24 former guest rooms, but the trust's current concept combines some rooms to create 18 self-contained apartments.
No apartments are ready for occupancy, and the purchase does not itself approve the conversion's final design.
The building has been vacant since its operator closed it in 2024; the purchase does not displace current motel guests.
The trust intends the apartments for households moving out of temporary accommodation under its locally funded allocation program.
Final eligibility rules, rents and application dates have not been published.
Trust director Dera Quill said, "A purchased building is an opportunity for homes, not eighteen keys we can hand out tomorrow."
The conversion must provide kitchens, improve insulation and revise fire-separation arrangements according to the trust's design brief.
The trust has commissioned an assessment of those works but has not fixed the renovation budget or selected a contractor.
The acquisition grant does not automatically fund every renovation expense.
A neighboring residents group supports reuse of the empty building but has asked how the trust will manage parking and support services.
Residents group secretary Olin Sare said, "We want to understand the daily arrangements, not argue about an empty building in the abstract."
The trust plans an on-site management office during staffed hours but has not proposed a round-the-clock staffed facility.
The former motel parking court will remain part of the site, with its final layout subject to the conversion design.
The project will use the existing building footprint rather than adding a separate apartment block in the first phase.
The trust will hold a public design meeting after the building assessment is complete.
The supplied records contain no completion date or forecast of the project's effect on the city's total housing waiting list.
The motel's former breakfast room is being considered for a shared laundry and meeting space, not a public restaurant.
The roadside lantern sign remains on the property, but the trust has not decided whether to retain it.
The seller has no continuing role in selecting future residents under the completed purchase agreement.
The trust says information will be published through local advice organizations as well as its own channels when applications are ready.

forbidden_additions: Twenty-four ready apartments, displaced current guests or an open application process.
Approved rents, final renovation funding or guaranteed completion.
A claim that the project will eliminate or quantify a reduction in the housing waiting list.
preserve: Completed acquisition distinguished from design, renovation and allocation stages.
The proposed conversion of room count into a smaller number of apartments.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
